# Coverage and boundaries

Source snapshot: Python `9c22a25c772c12b5d5f8057aabe6ac5cba7bcb20`, engine `42cc3d9714495b95577cf874e6c1c10174e9a831`.

The roster records 364 Python files plus `_common.py`. Its 37 topical examples are mapped below. The language corpus has 311 executed twins and 12 explicit adaptations or omissions. Four additional Python files under the nested `examples/` folder are two host-import fixtures and the two algebra demonstrations mapped separately below. Directory names follow the Python corpus; C language files are flat.

`native` identifies the corresponding C behavior. `adapted` identifies a different host implementation and states its limits. `gap` identifies behavior without a complete C or shared-engine service. These are coverage boundaries, not skipped binaries in `make check`.

## Additional boundaries

- Automatically maintained answer views remain a Python-owned maintenance algorithm; data/snapshot.c asserts only immutable collected answers.

Language source, runnable/definition boundaries, fixture bytes, source hashes and adaptations live in `corpus.json`. `tools/generate.py --check` checks every generated file and fixture. The large matespace workload streams and counts all 1,572,862 answers in C instead of materializing a single engine list.
